$comment: Demo data (CLAUDE.md 1.2). Twelve original problems for the Phase 3 prototype; hidden tests are not here, only their recorded outcomes in submissions.json.

problems.title: Missing tracks in a broadcast log
problems.statementMd:
A radio station plans a playlist: each entry is a track id and its length in seconds. The play log records what actually went on air. A planned track is **confirmed** when the log holds a line with the same track id and the same length.

Return the ids of planned tracks the log does not confirm, in playlist order.

A log line confirms at most one planned track. If the playlist holds the same track twice, the log must hold it twice too.
constraints: Track ids are 1 to 16 letters and digits

samples.note: One log line confirms one planned track.

problems.title: Merge overlapping bookings
problems.statementMd:
A meeting room's bookings arrive as `[start, end]` pairs in minutes since midnight, in no particular order. Two bookings that overlap or touch (one ends the minute the other starts) belong to one block.

Return the blocks, sorted by start.

problems.title: Sliding window maximum
problems.statementMd:
A sensor reports one temperature reading per second. For every window of `k` consecutive readings, report the highest reading in that window.

Return the maxima in window order. When there are fewer than `k` readings, return an empty list.

problems.title: Idempotent score submission
problems.statementMd:
A game client resends a score when the network drops, so the same submission can reach the leaderboard more than once. Each request carries a request key, a player and a number of points.

Process the requests in order. The first request with a key records its points. A later request with the same key and the same player and points is a retry: it records nothing. A later request with the same key but a different player or points is rejected as a conflict.

Return the points recorded per player, and the list of rejected request indexes.
constraints: Totals fit in a 64-bit signed integer

problems.title: Split match time to the millisecond
problems.statementMd:
A coach shares `total` milliseconds of playing time between players by weight. Each player's share is their weight's fraction of the total, rounded down to a whole millisecond. The milliseconds left over go one each to the players with the largest discarded fractions, ties broken by position.

The shares must add up to the total exactly.

problems.title: Token bucket rate limiter
problems.statementMd:
Each client of an API has a bucket that holds at most `capacity` tokens and refills at `rate` tokens per second, continuously. A request costs one token. A bucket starts full.

Given requests as `(timestamp in milliseconds, client)` sorted by time, return for each request whether it is allowed.

problems.title: Slowest endpoints in an access log
problems.statementMd:
Each line of an access log reads `METHOD PATH STATUS MILLISECONDS`. Lines that do not match this shape are skipped.

Return the `k` endpoints (method and path together) with the highest median response time, slowest first. Break ties by endpoint name.

samples.input:
k: 1
GET /a 200 30
GET /a 200 50
POST /b 201 45
broken line

problems.title: Fewest transfers between stations
problems.statementMd:
A rail network has numbered lines; each line is a list of stations it stops at. Riding a line between any two of its stops costs nothing; changing lines costs one transfer.

Return the fewest transfers needed to get from station `from` to station `to`, or `-1` when it cannot be done. Staying on the first line you board costs zero.

problems.title: Fewest tiles for a row
problems.statementMd: A tiler has unlimited tiles of each listed length. Return the fewest tiles that fill a row of exactly `length` units, or `-1` when no combination does. A row of length zero needs zero tiles.

samples.note: Three tiles of five; starting with twelve needs four.

problems.title: Two moves that cancel out
problems.statementMd: A robot on a rail logs each move as a signed number of steps. Given the log, return the indexes `[i, j]` with `i < j` of the first pair, in order of `j`, whose moves add up to zero. Return an empty list when there is none.

samples.note: A single zero has no partner.

problems.title: Top players by net points
problems.statementMd: Match events stream in as `(player, points)`. Return the `k` players with the highest net points, highest first, ties broken by player name. Penalties arrive as negative points and count against the total.

problems.title: The mirrored scorebook
problems.statementMd:
A league scorebook writes every point twice: once for the team that scored and once against the team that conceded, under a match id. A match is **consistent** when its scored and conceded points agree.

You receive entries in arrival order, some duplicated by a faulty scanner and some matches cut short.

1. Drop exact duplicate entries (same match, teams, points and sequence number).
2. Report every match that is still inconsistent, with the points it is off by.
3. For the consistent matches, return each team's closing tally.

Report matches in the order their first entry arrived.
constraints: Points are whole numbers up to 10^12

samples.input: [(m1, owls, foxes, 5, 1), (m1, owls, foxes, 5, 1), (m2, bears, owls, 2, 1)]
